ARABIC — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #2
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.

2. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.

3. When practising Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.

4. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.

5. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.

6. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.

7. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Only memorise without using the language
   C. Avoid speaking to classmates
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

8. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

9. When practising Reading Aloud: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud: Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Aloud: Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading: Library Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Sequencing Ideas and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing : Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
